page.layout: One page of text, left part of a printed page; a table of measures at the top (labels left, values centred and right), then a centred heading and running text at the right edge cut off. Margin note at the right side (Notae vulgares) inside the table area. Page number at the foot right: Q 4 (signature-like mark, read as printed). No running head.; One column of text at the right edge of the scan, consisting of fractions set in a stacked column with numerators and denominators, some with an italic word beside them; below, several lines of italic text running to the right edge, cut off at the line ends.

main_text.l: Duella uel binæ sextulæ. continet | 1 scrup:pri:40 sec.
main_text.p: Exempla harum appellationum sunt a nium lib:2.cap.14.& lib.18. cap.32.& alib
main_text.head: De erigendis cœli Figuris.
main_text.p: VT harum regularum, quas de Ascen differentijs & dierum tradidimus, utilitas ciatur, uno illustri exemplo in erectione figu cœli usum utrarumq; explicabimus & com mur.

page.notes: <note side="right">Notæ vulgares</note> Right edge cut off; text and notes are cut at the right margin. Some Greek-like/ornament figures (ɩo, the 6 and 5 are printed as numerals). Left-side text, the upper-right "Notæ uulgares" note reads "Notæ uulgares" as a marginal note. The table's Greek-style sign after Sextans is printed as "ɩo" (probably "10" in a decorative form). Fraction stacks are reproduced as lines; the numerator and denominator of each fraction are on separate printed lines, and the italic words at the right edge are cut off at their ends, so the completed forms are uncertain. The word "Plin." and the abbreviation "lib." are doubtful.
